angle: Basin attributes that explain cross-site mean nitrate in tile-drained corn belt catchments
verdict: PURSUE, but reframe what success looks like. This angle splits cleanly into two halves and they resolved very differently. The DATA half is solved and verified: the project's open item 'tile drainage - no data source identified' is closed. Two free, static, CONUS-wide, basin-aggregatable tile-drainage layers exist (AgTile-US 30 m raster via Figshare; USGS TILES92 via NHDPlusV2 COMID join), both computable at an arbitrary ungauged map pin with no local nitrate history and no discharge gauge, both fixing the known Iowa-clipped inner-join undercount for multi-state basins, and one of them reduces to a single hash lookup on the outlet COMID that this repo's existing NLDI code already returns. The EFFECT-SIZE half did not survive verification: NOT ONE verified source in this corpus links tile drainage fraction - or any other static basin attribute - to between-site nitrate variance in the Corn Belt. Every effect size in the requested attribute table (David 2010's tile=17%, Jones 2019's manure p<0.01, Schilling & Libra's 0.11 mg/L per % row crop, Pandit 2025's Shapley ranking with tile #1) is tier-3 unverified, and the only verification attempt that touched the numeric core - AgTile-US's 86.03%/91.1% accuracy - REFUTED the inference drawn from it, establishing that those figures are producer's recall on a detectability-biased positives-only sample, that the validation points also set a model threshold (in-sample), and decisively that AgTile-US errors are county-blocked by construction so basin aggregation does NOT average them out into a low-noise attribute. Pursue anyway, for three reasons that do not depend on the unverified effect sizes: (1) it targets the diagnosed deficit directly - between_r2 0.21 / between_rate_r2 0.24 is where essentially all headroom is; (2) it is the one feature CLASS that has ever worked on this project (geometry and static geography won; seven hydrologically-motivated temporal features failed); (3) it costs one static column, which is the only kind of thing estimable against ~19 independent basin families. But pre-register the test and temper the prior hard: both tile products are substantially deterministic functions of soil drainage class, slope and cropland, and Iowa tile is spatially concentrated in the Des Moines Lobe, so basin tile fraction may be largely spanned by lat/lon - already the #2 and #3 permutation-importance features - plus the 24 existing CDL columns. The honest benchmark is not 'current model + tile' but 'does tile survive CONDITIONAL on lat/lon under LOFO', and a null result would be weak evidence against the tile mechanism rather than strong. Expect a cheap, well-motivated shot with a real chance of zero incremental between_r2, not a fix.

findings.claim: The project's open gap 'tile drainage: dominant Iowa hydrologic control, not in the feature set, no data source identified' is now CLOSED. Two free, static, basin-aggregatable tile-drainage products verifiably exist and both are computable at an arbitrary ungauged map pin: (a) AgTile-US, a 30 m binary raster (1 = tile-drained cropland, 0 = undrained cropland) covering the full contiguous US for reference year 2017, CC-BY 4.0 on Figshare with no authentication; (b) TILES92, a percent-of-catchment-area-drained attribute keyed to NHDPlusV2 COMID inside the USGS 'Select Attributes for NHDPlus Version 2.1 Reach Catchments' release (ver. 5.0, Wieczorek et al., DOI 10.5066/F7765D7V), unauthenticated HTTPS GET. Both are CONUS-wide, so unlike the current Iowa-clipped CDL and N-surplus joins they do NOT under-count the out-of-state portions of the largest multi-state basins - this fixes that documented bug for the tile variable specifically (it does not fix it for CDL or N-surplus).
findings.effectSize: AgTile-US: 30 m, binary, CONUS, 2017, 22,340,442 ha tile-drained CONUS of which Iowa 5,706,831 ha (largest state). TILES92: 2,699,864 CONUS COMID rows, percent-of-area units, CAT_/ACC_/TOT_ aggregations. No nitrate effect size attaches to either - these are data-availability facts only.
sources: Valayamkunnath, Barlage, Chen, Gochis & Franz (2020), Scientific Data 7:257, doi:10.1038/s41597-020-00596-x - https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7406500/
Wieczorek, Jackson, Schwarz, Sekellick & Staub, ver. 5.0 (June 2025), DOI 10.5066/F7765D7V - https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5669a79ee4b08895842a1d47
findings.feasibilityAtN19: GOOD - the mildest form of the sample-size constraint. This adds ONE static scalar per basin (optionally three, one per existing distance bucket), evaluated against ~19 effective independent units. That is one degree of freedom, not a 300-basin architecture. Caution: a single spurious alignment across 19 units can still masquerade as a win, so report LOFO fold-level spread rather than a point estimate, and check stability under leave-one-family-out perturbation.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - fully. Both are static rasters/tables requiring nothing from the target site's own observations, no discharge gauge, and no monitored upstream neighbor. This is the cleanest deployment fit of any candidate in this angle.

findings.claim: CONCRETE INGEST TRAP, VERIFIED: the USGS release contains TWO tile tables and the obvious-looking 30 m one is the WRONG choice for Iowa. The Nakagaki (2016) 'early 1990s' derived table (ScienceBase item 58d9dec6e4b0543bf7fda70e, column CAT_TILES_Early90s) has CAT_NODATA == 100 (i.e. zero source coverage) for approximately 88% of CONUS catchments, and it writes the tile VALUE as 0.0 in those rows rather than null. A naive join therefore silently encodes 'no data' as 'no tile drainage' and injects a spatially structured false signal into exactly the between-site term the project is trying to repair. The sibling table TILES92 (item 57067469e4b03f95a075ad3e, columns COMID, CAT_TILES92, CAT_NODATA, ACC_TILES92, ACC_NODATA, TOT_TILES92, TOT_NODATA) has the same 2,699,864 rows with NODATA at 0.00% throughout and TOT_TILES92 > 0 for 2,488,931 COMIDs. Use TILES92 as the primary tile covariate; use Early90s only as a cross-check, and always gate on the paired NODATA column.
findings.effectSize: Early90s: CAT_NODATA==100 for ~88% of CONUS COMIDs (87.96% and 88.0% reported by two independent verifiers), TOT_NODATA==100 for 79.41%; one verifier measured TOT_NODATA 29.5% at a tested Iowa outlet. TILES92: NODATA identically 0.0 on all rows, no -9999 sentinel present.
sources: Verifier direct downloads of both tables under DOI 10.5066/F7765D7V
findings.feasibilityAtN19: N/A - this is a data-hygiene finding, not a modelling method. But it is disproportionately important at n=19: with only ~19 independent between-site units, a handful of basins falsely assigned tile=0 would be enough to manufacture or destroy an apparent between-site effect.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - and the trap applies equally at deployment. Any arbitrary pin whose basin falls in the ~88% uncovered fraction would receive a confident tile=0.0.

findings.claim: THE DEPLOYMENT PATH FOR THE USGS ATTRIBUTES IS ONE HASH LOOKUP, NOT A ZONAL-STATISTICS JOB. The TOT_ and ACC_ columns are ALREADY accumulated over the full upstream network at each reach, so an arbitrary map pin requires only: NLDI resolves the pin to a single outlet COMID, then one dictionary lookup into the attribute table. No basin decomposition into COMIDs, no raster processing, no local history. This repo already performs the NLDI call at /Users/isaac/dev/sustag/deploy/build_virtual_basin.py and /Users/isaac/dev/sustag/src/build/_make_basins.py. Independently confirmed end-to-end by a verifier: for Skunk River at Augusta IA, 110,403 of 110,403 NLDI-returned COMIDs matched the table (match rate 1.0000) and the outlet TOT_TILES value was 40.80%.
findings.effectSize: COMID match rate 1.0000 on a 110,403-COMID Iowa basin; outlet TOT_TILES 40.80%
findings.nBasins: 1 basin tested end-to-end (Skunk R. at Augusta, IA)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: N/A (engineering path). Note the corollary hazard below: because ingest is this cheap, the temptation to bulk-join hundreds of TOT_ columns is strong and must be resisted.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - this is the strongest verified deployment-compatibility result in the angle. It is the same NLDI operation the shipped product already performs.

findings.claim: REFUTED INFERENCE - do not claim that a basin-aggregated AgTile tile fraction is a low-noise attribute. The underlying numbers are exact (16,000 ground-truth points, 86.03% CONUS, 13.97% omission, Midwest 82.7-93.6%, Iowa 91.1% on 5,253 points), but three defects break the inference drawn from them. (1) POSITIVES-ONLY VALIDATION: the authors 'limited the tile drainage ground-truth identification mostly to fallow croplands where the tile drainage signature is easily detectable' - all 16,000 points are tile-drained locations, no confirmed non-drained controls, no confusion matrix, and 86.03 + 13.97 = 100.00 exactly. These are PRODUCER'S ACCURACY (recall) on a detectability-biased positive subsample; the commission/false-positive rate is unmeasured and unbounded by anything the paper reports. A map that over-painted tile across untiled cropland would score identically. (2) IN-SAMPLE: the same points that report accuracy also SET the model's 20% slope threshold ('to validate the AgTile-US AND to set the upper limit of slope in the geospatial model'). (3) DECISIVE - ERROR STRUCTURE IS COUNTY-BLOCKED: AgTile-US allocates USDA county-level census tile totals onto pixels, so errors are spatially correlated at county scale by construction and a basin spans few counties. Aggregation averages independent noise; it cannot average out systematic county-scale bias, and the paper states the census input itself carries 19.8% average error. The claim's conclusion is directionally wrong: basin-level aggregation inherits the county error essentially undiluted.
findings.confidence: high (this is a verified REFUTATION of a prior claim, not a new positive finding)
findings.effectSize: 86.03% is recall, not overall accuracy; commission error UNREPORTED; underlying USDA census tile estimates carry 19.8% average error which propagates undiluted to basin aggregates
findings.splitProtocol: in-sample map-accuracy assessment - the validation points also calibrated a model parameter. Explicitly NOT a predictive split and NOT comparable to the project's LOFO 0.820.
findings.feasibilityAtN19: This is the main reason to temper the prior. Adding one static predictor that carries roughly 20% county-correlated error against ~19 independent basin families risks fitting a census artifact rather than a tile signal. Any gain must be demonstrated under LOFO, never in-sample.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES the feature is computable at a pin; NO the accuracy figures do not license a per-basin noise estimate at that pin.

findings.claim: NO VERIFIED EFFECT SIZE EXISTS LINKING TILE DRAINAGE - OR ANY OTHER STATIC BASIN ATTRIBUTE - TO BETWEEN-SITE NITRATE VARIANCE. The AgTile-US paper is a Scientific Data DATA DESCRIPTOR containing zero nitrate concentrations, zero regressions of stream nitrate on tile fraction, and zero water-quality analysis of any kind. It establishes only that a defensible free covariate EXISTS. The USGS attribute release is likewise a data product, not a study, and reports no effect size and no split protocol. Every candidate effect size in the requested attribute table therefore rests on tier-3 unverified sources. This is a genuine hole in the evidence base, not a reporting gap: the angle can justify BUILDING the feature but cannot currently justify any expected magnitude of gain.
findings.effectSize: Zero nitrate effect sizes in any tier-1 verified source in this corpus
findings.feasibilityAtN19: The falsifiable test that survives verification is narrow and self-contained: adding a single static tile-fraction column should raise between_r2 (0.21) and between_rate_r2 (0.24) rather than within_r2 (0.42). That is estimable at 19 effective units. But it must be run - there is no literature prior to lean on.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: N/A

findings.claim: COLLINEARITY IS THE PRINCIPAL THREAT TO THE WHOLE ANGLE, AND IT IS VERIFIED MECHANISTICALLY. AgTile-US is not an observation of tile locations: it is a deterministic geospatial decision tree that allocates USDA 2017 county census tile acreage onto pixels using gSSURGO v2.0 soil drainage class (7 categories, iterated from D=7 downward) and SRTM slope (1% coarse then 0.1% fine steps, 20% ceiling) within an NLCD-2016 cropland mask. Basin tile fraction is therefore approximately 'flat, poorly drained cropland fraction' - a quantity the model may already carry via 8 CDL crop classes x 3 buckets plus lat/lon, which are the #2 and #3 permutation-importance features, especially since Iowa tile is spatially concentrated in the Des Moines Lobe. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (a) do NOT add AgTile fraction AND SSURGO hydrologic-soil-group/drainage-class AND mean basin slope as three separate features - they are the ingredients, not independent evidence; (b) the honest benchmark is a lat/lon-only baseline and a partial/orthogonalized contribution, not a raw add-one-column comparison; (c) compute VIF against the CDL bucket columns before concluding the feature failed, because a null result under high collinearity is weak evidence against the tile mechanism.
findings.effectSize: Inputs: USDA Ag Census 2017 county tile acreage; gSSURGO v2.0 drainage class (7 classes); NLCD 2016 cropland; SRTM slope (0-20% threshold). Aggregate CONUS deviation from census: -0.35% (22.34 vs 22.42 Mha) - close to tautological by construction, NOT independent validation.
findings.feasibilityAtN19: This is where n=19 bites hardest. A correlated static covariate can look informative in-fold and contribute nothing in transfer when only 19 independent units are available. Recommendation: test AgTile fraction as a REPLACEMENT for, or orthogonalized against, existing static geography - not simply as an addition.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES computationally, but the concern is statistical rather than operational.

findings.claim: PARTIALLY OFFSETTING THE COLLINEARITY CONCERN, AND THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT THAT AGTILE CARRIES REAL NEW INFORMATION: the AgTile thresholds are solved SEPARATELY FOR EACH COUNTY ('thresholds of slope and soil drainage properties were estimated separately for each county'), with each county's USDA Census tile acreage as the calibration target. Two counties with identical soil-drainage histograms, identical slope distributions and identical cropland fraction but different reported census tile acreage receive DIFFERENT thresholds and different tiled fractions. So basin tile fraction is f(soils, slope, cropland, COUNTY CENSUS TILE ACREAGE), and that last term is exogenous, farmer-reported, survey-derived information about human drainage investment that is not recoverable from any raster currently in the feature set. WITHIN a county AgTile variation is pure soil+slope and fully redundant; BETWEEN counties it carries real information - and since Iowa basins typically span multiple counties, the between-county component is precisely where any genuine between-site gain would come from. COROLLARY DEFECT: because thresholds are solved per county, AgTile-US has DISCONTINUITIES AT COUNTY LINES, and basin aggregates inherit a county-mosaic step artifact, worst for basins spanning many counties and for multi-state basins. Sanity-check basin tile fraction against county boundaries before trusting any between-site rank ordering derived from it.
findings.effectSize: County-specific (drainage-class, slope) thresholds; per-county census acreage is the only exogenous input. Its independent content is at COUNTY granularity - the 30 m grid is a rendering resolution, not an information resolution.
findings.feasibilityAtN19: Neutral-to-favorable. The information content is county-scale, and Iowa has 99 counties across ~19 basin families, so there is enough between-county contrast in principle. The clean ablation is AgTile-fraction VERSUS (drainage-class + slope + cropland-fraction) as competing feature sets under the same LOFO protocol - not both together.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES

findings.claim: DENOMINATOR AMBIGUITY - AgTile-US does not yield 'one number per basin'; it yields two materially different numbers and they are not interchangeable. Non-agricultural land is MASKED OUT, not coded 0. So (a) tile cells / total basin cells and (b) tile cells / agricultural cells are distinct quantities: (b) is drainage INTENSITY, the physically meaningful hydrologic control, while (a) conflates drainage with crop cover already captured by the 24 existing CDL features. Build and test both; (b) isolates the non-redundant component. Additional wrinkle: the mask is NLCD-2016 cropland, a DIFFERENT land-cover product from the CDL the project currently uses, and the paper reports NLCD-2016 underrepresents CONUS croplands by -18.15%, so cell-level agreement with existing crop features is imperfect and the ratio must never be taken against CDL crop-cell counts.
findings.effectSize: NLCD-2016 cropland deficit vs USDA census: -18.15% CONUS (state extremes for the CROPLAND MASK: WV -92.00%, NM -27.45%)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: Testing both denominators spends 2 columns instead of 1 against ~19 units. Prefer testing (b) drainage intensity first on hydrologic reasoning, and only add (a) if (b) shows signal.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - both denominators are computable from the raster over an NLDI-delineated basin.

findings.claim: AGTILE-US GEOGRAPHIC BIASES ARE REAL BUT LAND OUTSIDE IOWA - a prior concern that verification substantially DEFUSED for this project. The five worst state-level tile-area underestimates (NM -79.06%, WV -42.38%, MS -15.90%, OK -14.06%, TX -11.53%) are TILE-AREA errors, not cropland-mask errors, and none of those states is adjacent to or upstream of Iowa; Iowa's out-of-state basin tails run into MN, SD, NE, MO, IL and WI, and MN/IL/IN/OH sit in the well-performing group with tile-area deviation better than -0.25%. Iowa itself validates at 91.1% on 5,253 points (the densest per-state point count in the paper), and Iowa tile sits predominantly in the soil drainage classes AgTile captures best, while the documented weakness is concentrated in marginal drainage categories. Two prior speculations are therefore DROPPED as unsupported: that the bias would be 'worst in the discriminating middle needed for site ranking' (the paper reports no category-stratified error rate) and that it would be 'larger for multi-state basin tails' (null for Iowa's actual neighbours). The residual real limitation is NOT a systematic low bias but within-county spatial PLACEMENT noise plus the inherited 19.8% census error - worst for small single-county basins, partly averaging out for multi-county basins.
findings.effectSize: Iowa 91.1% recall on 5,253 points; Midwest tile-area deviation vs census better than -0.25%; problem states collectively hold under 0.11 Mha of tile; inherited census error 19.8%
findings.splitProtocol: in-sample map-accuracy assessment (see refutation finding above)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: Favorable - error should be treated as heteroscedastic noise (worse for small basins) rather than systematic bias, so it degrades power to detect a tile signal without biasing its sign.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES, with the caveat that a pin on a small single-county basin gets a noisier tile fraction than one on a large multi-county basin.

findings.claim: THE 2017-VINTAGE PARALLEL TO THE FAILED N-SURPLUS BROADCAST IS A CAUTION, NOT A PREDICTION OF FAILURE - but only if tile is entered as a STATIC attribute. AgTile-US is a single static 2017 snapshot (the paper's actual wording is 'The data deliver a static representation of U.S. tile drainage for the year 2017'; a previously circulated quote 'does not represent spatial or temporal changes in drainage installation' is a MISQUOTE and should not be used). Superficially this is the same 2017 endpoint as the N-surplus product whose forward-broadcast scored -0.166. The failure modes differ in kind: that experiment held a genuinely time-varying annual FLUX constant, whereas tile infrastructure is inertial on decadal timescales, so a 2017 constant is defensible across 2008-2026. Enter it as a time-invariant per-basin attribute ONLY - never as a per-day feature. The prior negative result is a reason to test rather than assume, and it does not predict failure here. Separate limitation: AgTile is binary presence/absence ('each 30-m grid identified as tile drained is entirely tile drained'), so it proxies drained AREA, not the drainage DENSITY/spacing that the project brief names as the dominant control.
findings.effectSize: Single vintage 2017; binary presence/absence, no sub-pixel drainage density, no drain spacing
findings.feasibilityAtN19: GOOD as a static column. Fails immediately if broadcast as a temporal feature - do not repeat that experiment.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES

findings.claim: THE USGS ATTRIBUTE RELEASE IS A 158-ITEM BUFFET AND THAT IS A HAZARD, NOT A BONUS, AT n=19. The release spans 13 themes (Best Management Practices, Chemical, Climate and Water Balance Model, Climate, Geology, Hydrologic, Hydrologic Modifications, Landscape, Population Infrastructure, Regions, Soils, Topographic, Water Use) and easily thousands of TOT_ columns, all joinable by COMID in one hash lookup. Bulk-joining them and letting XGBoost select creates a p >> 19 selection problem in which LOFO will select on noise across folds. RECOMMENDATION: pre-register a small handful chosen on hydrologic reasoning BEFORE seeing any LOFO score - tile drainage (TOT_TILES92), a soil/hydrologic-group term, base flow index, subsurface contact time, topographic wetness index, and one N-input term - and evaluate them as a fixed set. Do not sweep.
findings.effectSize: 158 child items (the true table/file count is higher - several items split CAT/ACC/TOT into separate zips), 13 themes, 2,699,864 COMID rows per table
findings.feasibilityAtN19: THIS IS THE n=19 FINDING. The binding constraint on this angle is not data availability - availability is now abundant - it is the number of static columns that can be honestly evaluated against ~19 independent between-site units. Budget 3-6 pre-registered attributes total.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES for all of them; the constraint is statistical, not operational.

findings.claim: OPERATIONAL CORRECTIONS TO THE USGS RELEASE THAT WILL OTHERWISE COST INGEST TIME. (1) LICENSE IS NOT CC0: the ScienceBase `rights` field is null for both parent and child items and no 'CC0'/'Creative Commons'/'public domain' string appears in the JSON or FGDC XML; FGDC accconst is 'None' plus a fitness-for-use disclaimer. Cite it as a USGS public-domain data release, free and unauthenticated - not as CC0. (2) NOT ALL ATTRIBUTES ARE STATIC SINGLE-EPOCH: many children are multi-epoch (NLCD across 8 years 2001-2019, ClimGRID monthly 1980-2020, housing density 1940-2010, NADP 1985-2014, per-year CDL items), which is a bonus for slowly-varying covariates. It IS true of the tile tables specifically. (3) THERE ARE FOUR SPATIAL COMPONENTS, NOT THREE - reach catchment, riparian buffer zone, network-accumulated catchment, and network-accumulated riparian buffer; packaging varies by item, so budget for per-item schema discovery rather than assuming one zip equals one 7-column table. (4) -9999 HAS TWO MEANINGS: in NODATA columns it means 100% no coverage; in ACC_/TOT_ value columns it means the reach is disconnected from the routing network (9,967 CONUS rows). (5) PARQUET COPIES ARE BROKEN - sciencebase.usgs.gov/manager/ URLs return an HTML app shell (HTTP 200, text/html, 4,255 bytes) and the bulk bundle returns 0-byte parquets; the zipped CSV is the working path. (6) FGDC METADATA BUG - the tile item's entity-attribute list labels the third variable 'ACC_TILES92' twice where the actual header says TOT_TILES92; parse the CSV header, not the XML. (7) STRUCTURAL CHURN RISK - parent provenance records '2026-03-26: The structure of this data release has been updated to support migration to a new USGS data system'; pin downloaded files locally and do not build a live-fetch dependency on the content-addressed ?f=__disk__<sha> URLs.
findings.effectSize: TILES92 zip 12,107,588 bytes (11.5 MiB), uncompressed 139,700,008 bytes (133 MiB), member file TILES92_CONUS.txt (comma-delimited, .txt extension)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: N/A (ingest engineering)
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES

findings.claim: THE USGS TILE LAYER IS A 1992 STATISTICAL SAMPLE, NOT A MAPPED DRAINAGE NETWORK - a caveat that materially limits what TILES92 can be claimed to measure. Its source is Wieczorek (2004) 'Estimated area of artificial drainage for the year 1992', derived from the 1992 National Resources Inventory Conservation Practice 606, an expanded statistical sample. The FGDC use constraint reads verbatim: 'One should use caution and read this document before using these data to estimate smaller areas. These data should not be used for site-specific evaluation, surveying, or engineering purposes. They should also not be used beyond the limits of the source data's scale.' Validation was a spot check only - 'Basin metrics were spot checked by randomly creating a set of basins across the country... Results demonstrated the process performed correctly' - with no quantitative accuracy statistic and 'No formal positional accuracy tests were conducted.' Iowa tile drainage has expanded materially since 1992. CONSEQUENCE: TILES92 supports a plausible RELATIVE RANKING of basins by drainage intensity; it does not support a defensible absolute drained-percentage. For the between-site ranking problem, relative rank is the quantity actually needed - so this is a usable but explicitly rank-only covariate. AgTile-US (2017) and TILES92 (1992) should be treated as two imperfect and non-interchangeable estimates of the same latent attribute.
findings.effectSize: 1992 vintage vs 2008-2026 nitrate record; no quantitative accuracy statistic published; agency constraint restricts use to multi-county/regional scale
findings.feasibilityAtN19: Usable, but it argues for testing BOTH tile products and treating agreement between them as the evidence, rather than trusting either alone at 19 units.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - Pandit, Golden, Christensen, Lane & Husic (2025, WRR 61(8), e2024WR039207, doi:10.1029/2024WR039207) is reported to be the closest published analogue to this project by scale (n=95 CONUS high-frequency nitrate sensor sites, 158,282 daily-averaged observations, 2007-2022, versus this project's ~85 sites and 160,074 site-days) and to report an LSTM median KGE of 0.60 under TEMPORAL validation versus only 0.18 under SPATIAL validation in unmonitored basins (0.34 restricted to Mississippi River Basin sites) - a ~0.42 KGE collapse that would independently reproduce this project's 'good timer, mediocre site-ranker' diagnosis at comparable n and indicate the cross-site level deficit is a field-wide limitation rather than an artifact of XGBoost or of the 19-family CV. The same study is reported to have explained long-term MEAN nitrate at those 95 sites with random forest plus Shapley values, ranking TILE DRAINAGE first, then roadway density, wetland cover, sand fraction, and precipitation - with attributes 1-4 all static and none present in this project's 68-feature set, while the sole meteorological entrant (precipitation) is this project's dead-last feature. THESE FIGURES WERE NEVER ADVERSARIALLY VERIFIED (article paywalled, HTTP 402 on all Wiley routes; numeric Shapley magnitudes were not retrievable even by the original extractor) and MUST NOT be used as the warrant for any decision. Use them only as a lead: this is the single most relevant paper to obtain in full text, and doing so is the highest-value next step in this angle.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - reported median KGE: temporal 0.60, spatial 0.18 CONUS / 0.34 MRB. Shapley rank order only; magnitudes not retrievable.
findings.splitProtocol: reported as spatial-holdout for the 0.18/0.34 figures (which if true WOULD be comparable in kind to this project's LOFO), temporal-holdout for 0.60; protocol for the random-forest/Shapley mean-nitrate analysis is UNKNOWN
findings.feasibilityAtN19: If the reported scale is accurate, this is the rare analogue whose evidence base is NOT hundreds of catchments - n=95 sites is the same order as this project's ~85, though the paper's independent-unit count under its spatial split is unknown and may be far below 95, exactly as ~85 sites collapse to 19 families here. Do not assume 95 independent units.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: The reported spatial-validation setting IS the ungauged-basin setting, which is why this source matters; but the reported KGE 0.18 would also be a warning that transfer skill in that setting is poor field-wide.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - MEASURED ON THIS PROJECT'S OWN DATA but never independently verified: area-weighted CAT_TILES92 aggregated over sensor-basin COMIDs correlated with site-level nitrate across n=46 joinable sites at Pearson r=0.516 (p=0.00024, r^2=0.266) and Spearman rho=0.605 versus site VIOLATION RATE, and r=0.466 (r^2=0.217) versus site mean daily-max nitrate; with log(basin area) as a covariate the tile coefficient remained significant (violation-rate model R^2=0.317, tile coef 0.0055, p=0.00138). Direction is positive as hydrologically expected. Attribute values spanned 0.03% to 67.79% of catchment area drained (mean 14.57%, std 19.16%), giving genuine cross-site dynamic range. TWO CRITICAL CAVEATS STATED BY THE ORIGINAL ANALYSIS ITSELF: this is an IN-SAMPLE cross-site correlation over all 46 sites with NO holdout, so r^2=0.266 is NOT comparable to the project's LOFO between_rate_r2 of 0.24 and will shrink under leave-one-family-out; and the 46 sites collapse to substantially FEWER than 19 independent basin families, so the effective independent n is well under 19 and the confidence interval on r is wide despite the small p-value. Treat as a promising pilot signal and a reason to run the LOFO test, NOT as evidence the feature works.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - violation rate r=0.516, r^2=0.266, Spearman 0.605; mean nitrate r=0.466, r^2=0.217; with log-area control R^2=0.317, tile coef 0.0055 (p=0.00138)
findings.splitProtocol: random-split / in-sample cross-site correlation, NO holdout - explicitly NOT comparable to LOFO numbers
findings.nBasins: 46 sensor basins, collapsing to fewer than 19 independent families

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - the strongest reported cross-site effect size for tile drainage specifically comes from David, Drinkwater & McIsaac (2010), J. Environ. Qual. 39:1657-1667, doi:10.2134/jeq2010.0115: a cross-sectional regression across 153 monitored Mississippi River Basin watersheds (1997-2006) reportedly explained 83% of the spatial variation in winter-spring nitrate-N yield, decomposed as river runoff x fertilizer-N interaction = 76%, TILE DRAINAGE EXTENT = 17%, sewage effluent = 7% - i.e. tile drainage was independently significant AFTER the runoff x fertilizer term was already in the model. The same source reportedly carries a directly relevant NEGATIVE result: conventional net nitrogen input / N-balance calculations were NOT a reliable predictor of riverine nitrate yields, and the term that worked was fertilizer N MULTIPLIED BY runoff rather than an N-surplus quantity entered additively. UNVERIFIED (extracted from the PubMed abstract and a university press release; Wiley full text returned HTTP 403 and the tile-drainage data source used could not be determined). THREE INDEPENDENT REASONS NOT TO PORT THE 17% AS A PRIOR: it is an IN-SAMPLE multiple regression with no spatial holdout, so 83% is an upper bound not comparable to LOFO; its predictors are COUNTY-level annual/seasonal census aggregates, giving no evidence about daily resolution; and its explanatory power comes from a CONUS-scale regime contrast (the same source reports export fraction varying ~30-fold, 0.05 lower Mississippi vs 0.3 upper Mississippi vs 1.4-4.2 for the tile-drained Embarras River, Illinois) whereas essentially ALL ~85 Iowa sensor sites sit inside the single high-yield tile-drained Corn Belt regime. The Iowa problem is WITHIN-regime discrimination, which is strictly harder and lower-signal than what this study resolved.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - 83% of spatial variation total; runoff x fertilizer N 76%, tile drainage 17%, sewage 7%; export fraction range 0.05 to 4.2
findings.splitProtocol: in-sample cross-sectional multiple regression, NO spatial holdout - NOT comparable to LOFO 0.820
findings.feasibilityAtN19: POOR AS A PRIOR. 153 watersheds spanning Minnesota to Louisiana is nearly 10x this project's independent-unit count and, more importantly, spans regimes this project does not. No coefficient or standard error for tile drainage is recoverable that could be ported. Its actionable content is directional only: tile extent is worth a column, and N surplus should be tried as an INTERACTION with a hydrologic transport term rather than additively.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: The attributes are static and pin-computable; but note the runoff term in the winning interaction is a DISCHARGE quantity unavailable at an ungauged pin (this project has discharge at only 22 of 85 sites, zero of 61 IWQIS sites). Any port would need a weather-derived runoff proxy, and rolling precip / water-balance proxies have ALREADY FAILED here (lofo_r2 0.013 vs 0.003).

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - LIVESTOCK/MANURE DENSITY IS THE MOST INTERESTING UNTESTED STATIC ATTRIBUTE, because the reported Iowa evidence says it beats the crop-area features the project already has. Jones, Drake, Hruby, Schilling & Wolter (2019), Ambio 48:1143-1153, reportedly found across 9 western-Iowa watersheds that 2017 flow-weighted-average NO3-N correlated significantly with MANURE N alone (p<0.01), with surplus N (p<0.01) and with commercial+manure N (p<0.01), but showed NO significant relationship with COMMERCIAL fertilizer N alone (verbatim: 'The FWA concentrations did not correlate with commercial N (p > 0.10)'), while corn+soybean area fraction was the WEAKEST significant predictor at only p<0.05. The reported mechanism is that commercial N application rates were near-uniform across basins (Rock 116, Floyd 112, nine-watershed average 117 kg/ha) despite FWA nitrate spanning 4.9-16.2 mg/L, so crop area structurally cannot discriminate basins whose loading differs through the manure term. Reported supporting spread: animal-unit density 0.45-5.00 AU/ha, with the two highest-density basins (Rock 5.00 AU/ha, Floyd 3.53 AU/ha) also the two highest-nitrate (11.5 and 16.2 mg/L) versus 7.3 mg/L for the other seven averaging 0.84 AU/ha - i.e. both high-density basins exceed the project's 10 mg/L violation threshold on an annual-average basis while the seven-basin average does not. UNVERIFIED AND FRAGILE: n=9 watersheds (~7 df), pure cross-sectional Pearson correlation, no multivariate model, no holdout of any kind, single year of nitrate data, and the paper reportedly does NOT report an R^2 for nitrate versus ANY predictor (Figure 4 shows scatter only), so NO usable partial effect size for cross-site nitrate variance exists even in the unverified record. The AU/ha-to-nitrate contrast is descriptive (2 basins vs 7), not a fitted statistic. NOTE ALSO an unresolved citation conflict in the corpus: this paper is given both as doi:10.1007/s13280-018-1137-5 and doi:10.1007/s13280-019-01150-9.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - manure N p<0.01, commercial N alone p>0.10 (an explicit negative), corn+soybean fraction only p<0.05; R^2=0.83 for surplus-N ~ manure-N versus R^2=0.14 for surplus-N ~ commercial-N (note this describes the DECOMPOSITION OF THE PREDICTOR, not nitrate prediction); FWA nitrate 4.9-16.2 mg/L across AU density 0.45-5.00 AU/ha
findings.splitProtocol: not-applicable - cross-sectional correlation, no holdout, no predictive model
findings.nBasins: 9 western-Iowa watersheds (1,049-8,350 km2), all draining to the Missouri River, single year (2017)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: The evidence base is n=9, SMALLER than this project's 19 families, so it is not a large-sample result that fails to transfer - it is a small-sample result that may not replicate at all. That cuts both ways: it is affordable to test (one static column), and it is the only Corn Belt attribute in this corpus that is reported to OUTPERFORM the crop-area features the project already encodes. Test it; expect wide uncertainty.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - county manure N and animal-unit density are static, publicly tabulated, and area-weightable to an NLDI-delineated basin with no local observation. Caveat: county resolution means a small basin may be dominated by one county.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED BUT LOGICALLY SOUND - THE N-SURPLUS 2017 CLIFF SHOULD BE ANSWERED BY REFRAMING SURPLUS AS A STATIC BASIN-RANK ATTRIBUTE, NOT BY FINDING A POST-2017 PRODUCT. Two parts. (a) The reported reality is that NO product extends past 2017: Falcone (2021, USGS OFR 2020-1153) terminates at 2017 because it is keyed to USDA Census of Agriculture years (1950...2012, 2017 - 15 time points, verified in the unverified record by CSV header inspection terminating at '-2017' columns); the related USGS release for 2002-2017 likewise stops at 2017; and gTREND-Nitrogen is itself published as 'Long-term nitrogen mass balance data for the contiguous United States (1930-2017)'. Any post-2017 continuation must be built from the 2022 Census of Agriculture directly. (b) THE REFRAME: the project's failed experiment (-0.166) broadcast a 2017 surplus FIELD FORWARD as a time-varying per-day feature. Entering a basin's N-input RANK once, as a time-invariant static attribute, is a DIFFERENT feature with a different failure mode, and the broadcast result does not falsify it. Three independent unverified strands support the reframe: a project-internal computation reporting Iowa county N inputs are highly rank-stable over two decades (Spearman versus 2017 of 0.910-0.969 for farm fertilizer N and 0.803-0.963 for manure N, across 99 Iowa counties, 1997-2012); a reported peer-reviewed precedent in which Gorski et al. (2024) used 'TOT_N97 - estimate of nitrogen from fertilizer and manure in 1997' as a fixed basin attribute in models spanning far later years; and Jones et al. (2019) reportedly obtaining significant relationships while regressing 2017 stream nitrate on 2012 census-derived N inputs, a 5-year offset. NONE of this is verified, and none of it supplies an effect size - the value of the static form remains untested and must be validated on this project's own LOFO folds.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - Iowa county rank stability Spearman 0.910-0.969 (fertilizer N) and 0.803-0.963 (manure N) versus 2017, n=99 counties. No nitrate effect size for the static form exists in any source, verified or unverified.
findings.nBasins: not-applicable (99 Iowa counties; no basin-level model fit was performed)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: GOOD - one static column, same shape as the tile feature. Note the reported agency use constraint cuts the right way: the FGDC useconst reads 'Data are best suited for use at multi-county or regional scales', which discourages fine temporal/single-county reading while endorsing aggregation - the opposite polarity from a broadcast time series.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - county tables area-weighted to an NLDI basin, or better, the COMID-keyed Sekellick & Sherr (2024) downscaling which joins with no county-to-basin reapportionment step.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - MANURE AND COMMERCIAL N ARE REPORTEDLY NOT REDUNDANT AND MANURE IS THE MORE DISCRIMINATING BETWEEN-SITE VARIABLE, which if true is directly on point for the between-site deficit. Project-internal computation over the Falcone files (already on disk at experiments/erin/data/N-P_from_fertilizer_1950-2017-july23-2020.xlsx and N-P_from_manure_1950-2017-july23-2020.xlsx) reportedly found for Iowa 2017: cross-county coefficient of variation 1.029 for manure N versus 0.404 for fertilizer N - 2.5x more between-unit spread - with Spearman correlation between the two of only 0.611, so they should enter as SEPARATE features rather than a single 'total N input'. Iowa 2017 manure N composition is reported as hogs 54.0%, cattle 39.7%, poultry 5.5%, other 0.8% (so a hog-specific term would carry most of the signal), and nonfarm/urban fertilizer N is only 0.56% of farm fertilizer N (so the nonfarm sheet can be dropped). Statewide totals reported as manure 4.633e8 kg versus farm fertilizer 1.123e9 kg. NOT VERIFIED. The reasoning that a feature with 2.5x higher between-unit variance is the better use of scarce degrees of freedom is sound in principle but the numbers themselves must be recomputed before being relied on.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - cross-county CV: manure N 1.029 vs fertilizer N 0.404; rank correlation between them 0.611; hogs = 54.0% of Iowa manure N; nonfarm = 0.56% of farm N
findings.feasibilityAtN19: Favorable in shape - it argues for spending the scarce between-site degrees of freedom on manure N rather than fertilizer N. But note a verified-record collinearity warning that applies here: the Falcone 2017 FERTILIZER values are random-forest model output whose 11 predictors include annual precipitation, ET, and county corn percent - so a 2017 fertilizer feature is not statistically independent of this project's existing precipitation and CDL crop features. The manure values do not have this problem (they are head-count x coefficient arithmetic).
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - CAUTION ON THE FALCONE 2017 FERTILIZER COLUMN SPECIFICALLY: it is MODEL OUTPUT, not measurement, and has a materially different error structure from every other column in the same file. AAPFCO state-level fertilizer tonnage for 2017 was never completed, so Falcone substituted a random forest with 11 predictors (percent county area in corn, pasture, N-fixing, small-grain and misc crops; fertilizer dollars divided by a price index; manure N or P kg; annual ET; annual precipitation; fertilized acres; population density) trained on 9,198 records (3,066 counties x 2002/2007/2012), 1,000 trees. Reported fit is OUT-OF-BAG r^2 = 0.948 (N) and 0.921 (P) - a RANDOM resample over county-years, explicitly NOT a spatial holdout, so it measures interpolation among neighbouring counties and is NOT comparable to any leave-one-basin-out number. County fertilizer EXPENDITURE IN DOLLARS dominates all agronomic and climatic predictors (%IncMSE 73.3 for N, roughly 2x the next predictor fertilized acres at 34.9), meaning the 2017 values are substantially a re-expression of Census-of-Agriculture dollars. Pre-2017 years are republished from earlier USGS products and are not model output of this kind. SEPARATE SCOPE LIMITATION: Falcone estimates nutrient INPUTS and does NOT subtract crop uptake or removal, so it is NOT a nitrogen-surplus product and is NOT a drop-in replacement for gTREND surplus; constructing a surplus from it would require separately obtaining county crop yields/removal from USDA NASS.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - RF OOB r^2 = 0.948 (N), 0.921 (P); n_train 9,198 county-years; 11 predictors; 1,000 trees; top predictor fertdolFPI %IncMSE 73.3
findings.splitProtocol: random-split (random-forest out-of-bag; explicitly NOT spatially held out) - do not compare to LOFO
findings.nBasins: not-applicable (3,066 counties x 3 training years; 0 basins)
findings.feasibilityAtN19: This is a reason to prefer the MANURE series over the fertilizer series as the static N attribute: manure is arithmetic from head counts, fertilizer 2017 is a model whose inputs overlap this project's existing features.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES, with the collinearity caveat.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - A CATCHMENT-LEVEL (NOT COUNTY-LEVEL) N-INPUT PRODUCT EXISTS AND IS THE BEST PIPELINE FIT: Sekellick & Sherr (2024), 'Nitrogen and phosphorus inputs from fertilizer and manure in the Continental United States, 2002-2017', USGS data release DOI 10.5066/P9WDBIXC, published 26 September 2024. It downscales the county-level estimates to NHDPlus Version 2.1 catchments keyed by COMID using NLCD land-cover classes, for 2002, 2007, 2012 and 2017. Eight CSV tables covering total N and total P from four source categories: agricultural fertilizer, CONFINED animal manure, UNCONFINED animal manure, and developed-land fertilizer. CONUS coverage, CSV plus XML metadata, bulk download, no authentication. OPERATIONAL VALUE: joins by COMID with NO county-to-basin areal reapportionment and no dependence on any observation at the target site, and the confined-vs-unconfined manure split is information neither the Falcone county tables nor gTREND surplus provides. UNVERIFIED - file listing, field names and license were not independently confirmed. CAVEAT ACKNOWLEDGED IN THE SOURCE CLAIM: it still ends at 2017 and does not solve the post-2017 cliff; it solves only the spatial-aggregation and multi-state-truncation problems.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - NHDPlusV2.1 COMID resolution; 4 years (2002, 2007, 2012, 2017); 8 tables; 4 source categories x N and P; CONUS. No model performance reported.
findings.feasibilityAtN19: GOOD - it slots into the same one-hash-lookup deployment path as TILES92 (verified for that release), so the marginal engineering cost after the tile work is near zero. Still spend degrees of freedom deliberately: pick ONE N term (confined manure N is the strongest candidate on the unverified Jones/Falcone reasoning), not all eight tables.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - COMID-keyed, static, no local observation required.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - THE REMAINING WISHLIST ATTRIBUTES ALL REPORTEDLY EXIST AS COMID-JOINABLE TABLES IN THE SAME (VERIFIED) USGS RELEASE, each with CAT_/ACC_/TOT_ and NODATA columns and CONUS coverage: (a) SUBSURFACE CONTACT TIME - 'the length of time it takes for water to drain along subsurface flow paths to the stream', units DAYS, from basin topography, soil porosity and hydraulic conductivity, Wolock (2014) per Wolock et al. (1997), item 56f96fc5e4b0a6037df06b12 - this is the requested subsurface residence/transit-time proxy; (b) BASE FLOW INDEX, percent, Wolock (2003), item 5669a8e3e4b08895842a1d4f; (c) DEPTH TO WATER TABLE below land surface, metres, Fan et al. (Rutgers, 2007), item 56f97456e4b0a6037df06b50; (d) MEAN ANNUAL NATURAL GROUNDWATER RECHARGE, mm/yr, 1951-1980 mean, Wolock (2003), item 56f97577e4b0a6037df06b5a; (e) TOPOGRAPHIC WETNESS INDEX ln(a/tan beta), Wolock & McCabe (1995), item 56f97be4e4b0a6037df06b70; (f) STATSGO2 HYDROLOGIC SOIL GROUPS as percent of catchment per group (USDA 2010), item 5728d93be4b0b13d3918a99f; (g) SSURGO SOIL RESTRICTIVE LAYER, estimated percent presence in the upper 25/35/45/55 cm of agricultural land, Nakagaki et al. (2012), item 572900afe4b0b13d3918aa64; plus riparian-buffer NLCD at 50 m and 100 m (items 57855ddee4b0e02680bf37bf, 64959e63d34ef77fcb01dcb7), percent watershed covered by waterbodies (57ab4009e4b05e859be1ad26), and mean flow-path distance to streams (5d1a1dfbe4b0941bde6025d2). The individual item IDs, units and provenance are UNVERIFIED (the parent release's structure, access and COMID key ARE verified). CRITICALLY: NO EFFECT SIZE ON NITRATE EXISTS FOR ANY OF THESE, in verified or unverified sources - availability is established, usefulness is entirely untested.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED item-level details; NO nitrate effect sizes reported for any of these attributes anywhere in this corpus
findings.feasibilityAtN19: THE DANGER ZONE. This makes dozens of static attributes trivially available against ~19 independent between-site units. Note also the verified finding that TOT_HGAD and TOT_HGBD - hydrologic soil groups whose DEFINITIONS are conditioned on artificial drainage ('high infiltration rate when artificially drained, very slow when not drained') - are a tile-drainage proxy obtainable independently of any tile map, so they are largely REDUNDANT with the tile feature rather than additive. Pre-register 3-6 attributes maximum on hydrologic reasoning before seeing any LOFO score.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES for all - static, COMID-keyed, no local observation required.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - A DIRECTLY RELEVANT PUBLISHED NEGATIVE RESULT ON POOLING NITRATE SITES. Gorski et al. (2024, doi:10.1029/2023WR036591) reportedly state: 'Developing a single model for all sites reduced performance at several locations with distinct characteristics, suggesting that there is a threshold of dissimilarity beyond which more data does not improve the model', adding 'While many deep learning studies have shown that national or even global models can outperform local models, it is not clear that this is true for water quality constituents.' Accuracy at poorly performing sites was reportedly improved instead by GROUPING sites with similar characteristics (their data release carries a 'cluster' and a 'hydro_terrane' label per site). If true this is peer-reviewed evidence that the CAMELS-style 'one big multi-basin model wins' result does not automatically hold for nitrate. TWO ESSENTIAL PROTOCOL CAVEATS, both stated in the source claim: the paper's headline median KGE 0.66 comes from SINGLE-SITE models 'trained and tested at a single location' with no site ever spatially held out, so it is NOT comparable to this project's LOFO numbers and provides NO evidence of transfer to an unmonitored basin; and all 46 sites are USGS gauges with daily discharge (NWIS 00060) as a REQUIRED model input, making the entire design inapplicable to an arbitrary ungauged pin. The magnitude of the pooling drop is not recoverable (full text Cloudflare-blocked). ACTIONABLE FORM FOR THIS PROJECT: with 19 independent families, splitting into similarity clusters leaves ~4-6 families per cluster, almost certainly too few to fit separate models - so the usable version is cluster or hydro-terrane MEMBERSHIP AS A STATIC FEATURE, not as a model partition.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - single-site median KGE 0.66; pooled model 'reduced performance at several locations'; drop magnitude not recoverable
findings.splitProtocol: temporal-holdout within sites (single-site train/validation/test periods); NO spatial holdout anywhere in the study - NOT comparable to LOFO 0.820
findings.feasibilityAtN19: The clustering approach as published is INFEASIBLE at n=19 - it would leave 4-6 families per cluster. Only the feature-membership variant is affordable, and that spends a degree of freedom on a categorical with few levels.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: NO for the published design - every site is a gauge and daily discharge is a required input, which this project has at only 22 of 85 sites and 0 of 61 IWQIS sites. Only the static attribute list and the cluster-membership idea transfer.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - ROW-CROP PERCENTAGE IS THE BEST-ESTABLISHED IOWA BETWEEN-SITE PREDICTOR IN THE LITERATURE, BUT IT IS THE ONE ATTRIBUTE THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS. Schilling & Libra (2000), J. Environ. Qual. 29(6):1846-1851, reportedly found mean annual stream NO3-N directly related to watershed row-crop percentage at p<0.0003 across 15 large Iowa watersheds (1,002-2,774 km2) and 10 small ones (47-775 km2) sampled 1996-1998, with essentially the SAME regression slope of 0.11 mg/L per percentage point in BOTH size classes - yielding the rule of thumb that mean annual Iowa stream nitrate approximates row-crop-percent x 0.1. Slope stability across a ~50x span in basin area would be evidence the attribute is scale-transferable, which matters for a virtual sensor applied to arbitrary basin sizes, and n=25 watersheds is the same ORDER as this project's 19 families rather than a 300-basin result. THREE REASONS THIS IS LOW-VALUE HERE DESPITE BEING THE CLEANEST REPORTED EFFECT SIZE: (1) the project ALREADY encodes 8 CDL crop classes x 3 distance buckets, so row-crop fraction is present and has not closed the between-site gap; (2) the r^2 / explained-variance values could NOT be determined from any open source (Wiley, USGS pubs page, ProQuest and ResearchGate all returned HTTP 403; OpenAlex reports only p<0.0003 and slope 0.11), so how much cross-site variance it explains is genuinely unknown; (3) the source claim itself notes more recent work reportedly reports a substantially different slope near 0.4 mg/L per 10% row crop, so 0.11 should be treated as unreliable and re-estimated on this project's own families. A REPORTED PARTIAL NEGATIVE also matters: in the 10 small watersheds row-crop spanned 28-87% but nitrate spanned only 3.0-10.5 mg/L with a FLOOR of 3.0, versus a 0.5 mg/L floor at 24% row crop in the large watersheds - the same slope does not reproduce the same intercept behaviour at small scale, implying an additional unidentified basin attribute sets the low end in large basins.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - slope 0.11 mg/L NO3-N per 1% row crop, p<0.0003; large basins row crop 24->87% and NO3-N 0.5-10.8 mg/L; small basins 28-87% and 3.0-10.5 mg/L; r^2 UNRECOVERABLE
findings.feasibilityAtN19: The evidence base (n=25) is genuinely comparable to n=19, which is unusual and valuable - it is one of very few Corn Belt between-site findings NOT resting on hundreds of catchments. But it points at a feature the project already has, so its practical value is as a SANITY CHECK: if the model's existing CDL features are not reproducing an approximately 0.1 mg/L-per-percent row-crop between-site gradient across the 19 families, that is a diagnostic that something is wrong with the aggregation, not that a new attribute is needed.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES - already implemented.

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED - ALTERNATIVE/INFERIOR TILE PRODUCTS EXIST AND SHOULD NOT BE SUBSTITUTED FOR THE TWO RECOMMENDED ONES. Nakagaki & Wieczorek (2016), 'Estimates of subsurface tile drainage extent for 12 Midwest states, 2012' (DOI 10.5066/F7W37TDP) is also 30 m and 20 years more recent than the 1992 NRI layer, but it disaggregates from STATE-level 'land drained by tiles' acreages from the 2012 Census of Agriculture rather than county-level totals, so it reportedly carries LESS spatial information for distinguishing basins WITHIN Iowa despite its newer vintage; it also covers only 12 states (SD, NE, KS, MN, IA, MO, WI, IL, MI, IN, OH, KY), so basins extending outside them would be truncated - reintroducing exactly the multi-state truncation problem the CONUS products fix. The companion CONUS product Nakagaki, Wieczorek & Qi (2016), 'Estimates of Subsurface Tile Drainage Extent for the Conterminous United States, early 1990s' (DOI 10.5066/F7RB72QS), built from Sugg (2007) county acreages, NLCD 2011 cropland and STATSGO2 poorly drained soils, is the raster whose NHDPlus-aggregated form is the VERIFIED-DEFECTIVE Early90s table (~88% of CONUS catchments have zero source coverage encoded as 0.0). UNVERIFIED at the source records (ScienceBase returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; specs recovered from the USGS data-catalog mirror), and the CC0 license attributed to them should be treated with the same skepticism as the CC0 attribution that was DISPROVEN for the parent USGS attribute release.
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED - 12-state product: 30 m, 2012 Ag Census, STATE-level disaggregation, 12 states only. CONUS early-90s product: 30 m, cell values in square metres of estimated tile drainage, Sugg (2007) county acreages.
findings.feasibilityAtN19: N/A - the recommendation is to NOT spend a column on these. Use AgTile-US (2017, county-calibrated, CONUS) and TILES92 (COMID-native, complete coverage) instead.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: The 12-state product FAILS for pins whose basins extend outside the 12 states; the CONUS early-90s product is pin-computable but has the zero-fill coverage defect.

datasets.name: AgTile-US - 30 m tile-drained cropland map of the contiguous United States (Valayamkunnath, Barlage, Chen, Gochis & Franz 2020)
datasets.url: Primary data: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.11825742 (direct file: https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/23079140). Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-00596-x. Code: https://github.com/NCAR/AgTile-US. Community GEE mirror (prototyping only): projects/sat-io/open-datasets/agtile/AgTile-US via https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/tile/
datasets.resolution: 30 m, binary (1 = tile-drained cropland, 0 = undrained cropland; non-agricultural land is MASKED OUT, not coded 0). Albers NAD83. Uncompressed CONUS is 153,810 x 96,815 uint8, approximately 14.9 GB - clip before storing.
datasets.years: Single static vintage: 2017 (USDA 2017 Census of Agriculture county tile acreage, gSSURGO v2.0 drainage class, NLCD 2016 cropland mask, SRTM slope). NO time dimension, no annual update.
datasets.access: Figshare bulk download, anonymous HTTP, NO authentication (verified by anonymous HTTP 206 range download). AgTile-US-TIFF.zip is 126 MB compressed. GeoTIFF and NetCDF-4. AVOID the Google Earth Engine path for production: it requires a Google account and an Earth-Engine-registered Cloud project (authentication), and Earth Engine's free tier is noncommercial/research only - commercial or operational applications require a paid Google Cloud Earth Engine subscription. The CC-BY license governs the raster, not the platform serving it. The GEE asset is also an ee.Image (not an ImageCollection) maintained as a third-party community mirror by the sat-io project, with no persistence guarantee from NCAR or Google.
datasets.license: CC-BY 4.0 for the data (confirmed in the Figshare API license field), metadata CC0. Free for commercial use with attribution when self-hosted.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES - full CONUS (65 20'46"W to 127 53'14"W, 22 51'41"N to 51 36'17"N). Covers every out-of-state tail of Iowa basins (MN, SD, NE, MO, IL, WI), all of which sit in the product's well-performing Midwest group. This directly fixes the documented Iowa-clipped inner-join undercount FOR THE TILE VARIABLE ONLY - the CDL and N-surplus joins remain truncated.
datasets.whyUseful: Tile drainage is the project brief's named dominant Iowa hydrologic control and is currently absent from the feature set. This is a purely STATIC between-site covariate, which is the only feature class that has ever produced gains on this project (geometry and static geography won; seven hydrologically-motivated temporal features failed). Iowa is the most tile-drained state (5,706,831 ha) with the paper's densest validation (91.1% recall on 5,253 points).
datasets.howToIncorporate: Bulk-download AgTile-US-TIFF.zip once from Figshare, clip to the Iowa-plus-upstream footprint, and compute per-basin statistics locally with rasterio or exactextract over the existing NLDI-delineated basin polygons - reusing the existing basin-cell aggregation machinery. Create TWO distinct features and test them separately, because they are not interchangeable: (1) tile_frac_basin = tile cells / total basin cells; (2) tile_frac_ag = tile cells / agricultural (unmasked) cells, which is drainage INTENSITY and is the physically meaningful control that does not merely restate crop cover. NEVER compute the denominator against the project's CDL crop-cell counts - the mask is NLCD-2016, a different product. Add ONE basin-wide feature first, not three distance-bucketed copies: the bucketed version spends three degrees of freedom on a between-site term with only ~19 independent units, and the riparian-bucket precedent (CLF +0.039 PR-AUC but REG worse) shows bucketing static geography is not reliably free. Enter as a TIME-INVARIANT column only - never broadcast per-day. Before interpreting any result, regress the basin tile fraction on lat, lon, log_basin_area and the CDL bucket features and report the residual R^2; the honest ablation is AgTile-fraction VERSUS (drainage class + slope + cropland fraction) as competing feature sets under the same LOFO protocol, not both together.
datasets.limitations: MODELED, NOT OBSERVED - a deterministic decision tree that allocates county census tile acreage by soil drainage class and slope, so basin tile fraction is largely a smooth function of soils, slope and cropland and may be substantially collinear with lat/lon (already the #2 and #3 features by permutation importance), especially since Iowa tile is concentrated in the Des Moines Lobe. The 86.03% CONUS / 91.1% Iowa figures are PRODUCER'S RECALL on a positives-only, detectability-biased sample (fallow fields where tile signatures are visible), not overall accuracy - commission error is unmeasured and unbounded by anything the paper reports - and the same points also set the model's 20% slope threshold, making the assessment in-sample. Errors are COUNTY-BLOCKED by construction, so basin aggregation does NOT average them out, and the inherited USDA census error (19.8% average) propagates essentially undiluted. County-specific thresholds create DISCONTINUITIES AT COUNTY LINES that basin aggregates inherit as a step artifact. Binary presence/absence only - it proxies drained AREA, not drainage DENSITY or drain spacing. The -0.35% agreement with census totals is near-tautological (the census is the calibration target) and is NOT independent validation. The NLCD-2016 mask underrepresents CONUS cropland by -18.15%. Contains ZERO water-quality analysis, so it can never be cited as evidence that tile fraction explains between-site nitrate variance.

datasets.name: TILES92 - percent subsurface drainage per NHDPlusV2 catchment, within 'Select Attributes for NHDPlus Version 2.1 Reach Catchments and Modified Network Routed Upstream Watersheds for the Conterminous United States' (Wieczorek, Jackson, Schwarz, Sekellick & Staub, ver. 5.0, June 2025)

datasets.years: Single epoch: 1992 (source is Wieczorek 2004, derived from the 1992 National Resources Inventory Conservation Practice 606).
datasets.access: Unauthenticated HTTPS GET of a zipped CSV from sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/<itemid>. Zip is 12,107,588 bytes (11.5 MiB); uncompressed 139,700,008 bytes (133 MiB); member file is TILES92_CONUS.txt, comma-delimited with a .txt extension. Parquet copies are listed but BROKEN - sciencebase.usgs.gov/manager/ URLs return an HTML app shell and the bulk bundle returns 0-byte parquets. Use the CSV zip.
datasets.license: USGS public-domain data release, free, no authentication. NOT CC0 - the ScienceBase `rights` field is null and no CC0 / Creative Commons / public-domain string appears in the JSON or FGDC XML; accconst is 'None' plus a fitness-for-use disclaimer. Cite it as a USGS public-domain release, not as CC0.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES - full CONUS COMID coverage, and CAT_NODATA/ACC_NODATA/TOT_NODATA are 0.00% throughout this table, with TOT_TILES92 > 0 for 2,488,931 COMIDs. Verified end-to-end on an Iowa basin: 110,403 of 110,403 NLDI-returned COMIDs matched (rate 1.0000).
datasets.whyUseful: It is the SAME latent attribute as AgTile-US from an independent lineage and vintage, so agreement between the two is stronger evidence than either alone at n=19. Operationally it is the cheapest possible feature to deploy: TOT_ is already accumulated over the full upstream network, so an arbitrary map pin needs only NLDI to resolve the outlet COMID plus one hash lookup - no basin decomposition, no zonal statistics, no raster processing.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Create feature `tot_tiles92` = the TOT_TILES92 value at the basin outlet COMID (one hash lookup on the COMID this repo's NLDI call already returns at /Users/isaac/dev/sustag/deploy/build_virtual_basin.py and /Users/isaac/dev/sustag/src/build/_make_basins.py). Optionally create `cat_tiles92_wmean` as the area-weighted mean of CAT_TILES92 over the basin's constituent COMIDs where a full decomposition exists. Parse the CSV HEADER, not the FGDC XML - the XML entity-attribute list has a bug labeling the third variable 'ACC_TILES92' twice where the header says TOT_TILES92. Pin the downloaded file locally; do not build a live-fetch dependency on the content-addressed ?f=__disk__<sha> URLs, which can change (parent provenance records a 2026-03-26 migration to a new USGS data system). PREREQUISITE: resolve the reported gap that only 46 of 85 basins currently carry COMIDs - 3 basin parquets lack a 'comid' column and ~36 are stored as a single dissolved polygon with comid=None. Decompose them via spatial intersection against the NHDPlusV2 catchment layer or via NLDI navigation before running the ablation, or the test will be underpowered.
datasets.limitations: 1992 vintage against a 2008-2026 nitrate record, and Iowa tile drainage has expanded materially since. It is an expanded STATISTICAL SAMPLE (NRI CP-606), not a mapped drainage network. The FGDC use constraint reads verbatim: 'These data should not be used for site-specific evaluation, surveying, or engineering purposes. They should also not be used beyond the limits of the source data's scale.' Validation was a spot check only, with no quantitative accuracy statistic and no formal positional accuracy test. CONSEQUENCE: this supports a plausible RELATIVE RANKING of basins by drainage intensity, not a defensible absolute percentage - acceptable here, since relative rank is exactly what the between-site problem needs. Note also that the NODATA columns in THIS table are identically 0.0 and therefore carry no coverage diagnostic; the release-wide 'NODATA makes coverage auditable' argument is vacuous for this specific table and must be re-checked per table.

datasets.name: AVOID - CAT_TILES_Early90s (Nakagaki, Wieczorek & Qi 2016 tile raster, as aggregated to NHDPlusV2)
datasets.resolution: NHDPlusV2 catchment, COMID-keyed; underlying raster 30 m with cell values in square metres of estimated tile drainage.
datasets.years: Early 1990s (Sugg 2007 county acreages, NLCD 2011 cropland, STATSGO2 poorly drained soils).
datasets.access: Same unauthenticated ScienceBase zipped-CSV path as TILES92.
datasets.license: USGS public domain (the CC0 attribution circulating for this item should be treated with the same skepticism as the CC0 attribution disproven for the parent release).
datasets.coversMultiState: Nominally CONUS, but effectively NO - CAT_NODATA == 100 (zero source coverage) for approximately 88% of CONUS catchments and TOT_NODATA == 100 for 79.41%.
datasets.whyUseful: Listed only so it is not mistakenly chosen. It is the obvious-looking headline 30 m tile layer and it is the WRONG one for Iowa.
datasets.howToIncorporate: DO NOT USE as a primary feature. If used at all as a cross-check, gate strictly on the paired NODATA columns and mask any value where NODATA exceeds a small threshold. Note the two tile products correlate only r=0.688 where both have data (unverified), so they are NOT interchangeable.
datasets.limitations: THE CRITICAL TRAP: this table writes the tile VALUE as 0.0 rather than null where the source grid is absent. A naive ingest therefore encodes 'no data' as 'no tile drainage' and injects a systematic, spatially structured false signal into exactly the between-site term the project is trying to repair. Reported project-internal measurement (unverified) found 25.6% of sensor basins with 100% area-weighted NODATA and 42.7% above 50%, median 95.84%.

datasets.name: Falcone (2021) - Estimates of county-level nitrogen and phosphorus from fertilizer and manure, 1950 through 2017, conterminous United States (USGS OFR 2020-1153)
datasets.url: Report: https://doi.org/10.3133/ofr20201153 and https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2020/1153/ofr20201153.pdf. Data release: https://doi.org/10.5066/P9VSQN3C, ScienceBase item 5ebad56382ce25b51361806a
datasets.resolution: County (3,066 CONUS counties, 99 in Iowa), keyed on STCOFIPS. Units are kilograms of elemental N and P (P2O5 converted by factor 0.437).
datasets.years: 15 USDA Census of Agriculture years: 1950, 1954, 1959, 1964, 1969, 1974, 1978, 1982, 1987, 1992, 1997, 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017. TERMINATES AT 2017 - no post-2017 continuation exists.
datasets.access: Direct unauthenticated HTTP GET from ScienceBase. Plain CSV text files 300-590 KB each (fert-farm-1987-2017.txt, fert-nonfarm-1987-2017.txt, fert-total-1950-1982.txt, manure1950.txt ... manure2017.txt), plus two XLSX (1.5 MB fertilizer, 14 MB manure) and model_archive.zip. NOTE: these exact files are ALREADY ON DISK in this repo at experiments/erin/data/N-P_from_fertilizer_1950-2017-july23-2020.xlsx and experiments/erin/data/N-P_from_manure_1950-2017-july23-2020.xlsx - no download required. (One source reports ScienceBase returning HTTP 403 to automated fetch; confirm the file listing manually if re-downloading.) All access details are UNVERIFIED.
datasets.license: Reported as CC0 1.0 / USGS public domain, FGDC accconst 'None'. UNVERIFIED - and note that the analogous CC0 attribution was DISPROVEN for the USGS NHDPlus attribute release, so verify before relying on it.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES - all 3,066 CONUS counties, so Iowa and every multi-state basin tail (MN, SD, NE, MO, IL, WI) are covered by the same product. Does not suffer the Iowa-boundary truncation of the current gTREND grid inner-join.
datasets.whyUseful: Supplies the manure-versus-commercial N split the research question asks for, as separate files with separate fields - the decomposition the current gTREND surplus features do not provide. Reported (unverified) analysis says manure N has 2.5x the between-county spread of fertilizer N (CV 1.029 vs 0.404) with only 0.611 rank correlation between them, making manure N the better use of scarce between-site degrees of freedom.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Create ONE static feature `manure_n_kg_per_km2` = area-weighted intersection of county Total_N_kg (manure2017.txt or, better, a multi-year mean over 2002/2007/2012/2017 to reduce single-census noise) against the basin polygon, divided by basin area. Optionally a second `hogN_frac` since hogs are reported as 54.0% of Iowa manure N. Enter as a TIME-INVARIANT column - the basin's static N-input RANK - NOT as a broadcast time series; the failed forward-broadcast experiment (-0.166) tested the latter construct and does not falsify the former. Drop the nonfarm/urban fertilizer sheet (reported 0.56% of farm N in Iowa). PREFER the manure series over the 2017 fertilizer series (see limitations).
datasets.limitations: COUNTY RESOLUTION is far coarser than the 30 m cell pipeline; a 1,000-2,000 km2 Iowa basin typically intersects only 2-5 counties, so this is usable as ONE basin-level scalar and NOT as a per-distance-bucket feature, and for small basins a single county may dominate. The agency's own use constraint reads 'Data are best suited for use at multi-county or regional scales'. IT IS AN INPUTS PRODUCT, NOT A SURPLUS PRODUCT - it does NOT subtract crop uptake or removal, so it is not a drop-in replacement for gTREND surplus; building a surplus would require separately obtaining county crop yields from USDA NASS. The 2017 FERTILIZER column specifically is random-forest MODEL OUTPUT (AAPFCO 2017 tonnage was never completed), with OOB r^2 0.948 measured by RANDOM resampling over county-years, explicitly NOT a spatial holdout, and its 11 predictors include annual precipitation, ET and county corn percent - creating direct collinearity with this project's existing weather and CDL features. County fertilizer expenditure in dollars dominates that model (%IncMSE 73.3), so the 2017 fertilizer field is substantially a re-expression of census dollars. USDA withholds county livestock counts for disclosure: withheld hog counties grew 26 (1974) to 212 (1992) to 576 (2012), and 515 were backfilled from prior censuses in 2017 - concentrated in exactly the high-confinement counties that matter most for Iowa nitrate. Broomfield County, Colorado is omitted entirely. ALL DETAILS UNVERIFIED.

datasets.name: Sekellick & Sherr (2024) - Nitrogen and phosphorus inputs from fertilizer and manure in the Continental United States, 2002-2017 (COMID-level downscaling)
datasets.resolution: NHDPlus Version 2.1 catchment, keyed by COMID - NOT county. Downscaled from county estimates using NLCD land-cover classes.
datasets.access: Eight CSV tables plus XML metadata, bulk download, no authentication. Published 26 September 2024. UNVERIFIED - file listing and field names were not independently confirmed.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES - CONUS, so multi-state basins are complete.
datasets.whyUseful: BEST PIPELINE FIT of the N-input products. Four source categories x N and P: agricultural fertilizer, CONFINED animal manure, UNCONFINED animal manure, and developed-land fertilizer. The confined-vs-unconfined manure split is information neither the Falcone county tables nor gTREND surplus provides, and it is the physically meaningful distinction for Iowa hog confinement. Because it is COMID-keyed it joins with NO county-to-basin areal reapportionment step and reuses the exact deployment path verified for TILES92.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Create ONE feature `confined_manure_n_tot` = the TOT_ (or catchment-accumulated) confined-manure-N value at the basin outlet COMID, from the 2017 table, normalized by basin area - one hash lookup on the COMID NLDI already returns. If a second column can be afforded, add `ag_fertilizer_n_tot` separately rather than summing them into a single 'total N input', on the reported (unverified) finding that manure and fertilizer are only 0.611 rank-correlated. Consider using the mean across 2002/2007/2012/2017 rather than the 2017 snapshot alone, to express the basin's stable RANK rather than one census year. Time-invariant column only.
datasets.limitations: Ends at 2017 - solves the spatial-aggregation and multi-state-truncation problems but NOT the post-2017 cliff. It is a downscaling of the same county estimates, so within-county spatial variation is a modeled artifact of NLCD land cover rather than an observation, and it inherits every accuracy limitation of the Falcone/Brakebill/Gronberg county lineage including the 2017 fertilizer model-output problem. NO effect size on nitrate is reported - it is a data release, not a study. ALL DETAILS UNVERIFIED.

datasets.name: USGS 'Select Chemical Attributes: Nitrogen and Phosphorous Estimates from Fertilizer and Manure, 2012' (COMID-level, within the same NHDPlus attribute release)
datasets.resolution: NHDPlusV2 catchment, COMID-keyed, with CAT_/ACC_/TOT_ plus NODATA columns. Units kilograms, -9999 as NODATA.
datasets.years: 2012 only - a single snapshot, no time series.
datasets.access: Eight zipped CSVs, unauthenticated HTTPS GET from ScienceBase. UNVERIFIED.
datasets.license: Reported CC0. UNVERIFIED - and disproven for the parent release, so verify.
datasets.whyUseful: Supplies the manure-vs-commercial split at COMID with a ROW-CROP-RESTRICTED variant, which no other product offers: FarmN2012/FarmP2012 = commercial fertilizer on agricultural land (Brakebill et al. 2017); TN2012/TP2012 = manure on agricultural land (Gronberg et al. 2017); RCFN2012/RCFP2012 and RCTN2012/RCTP2012 = the same quantities restricted to ROW CROP land specifically. The row-crop weighting is closer to the actual loading pathway than whole-county totals.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Create `rc_manure_n_tot` from RCTN2012 at the outlet COMID (row-crop-restricted manure N, area-normalized) as the single highest-information N column available at COMID resolution. This is an alternative to, not an addition to, the Sekellick confined-manure feature - pick one, do not spend two degrees of freedom on near-duplicates.
datasets.limitations: SINGLE YEAR 2012 ONLY, and the underlying Brakebill fertilizer series itself ends in 2012 - five years EARLIER than the gTREND surplus product that already ends in 2017. So this makes the temporal-coverage problem worse, not better, and its ONLY defensible use is the static-basin-rank framing. ALL DETAILS UNVERIFIED.

datasets.name: USGS Select Attributes for NHDPlusV2.1 - remaining wishlist attributes (contact time, base flow index, water table depth, recharge, TWI, hydrologic soil groups, soil restrictive layer, riparian buffers)

Reported child items: contact time 56f96fc5e4b0a6037df06b12; base flow index 5669a8e3e4b08895842a1d4f; depth to water table 56f97456e4b0a6037df06b50; groundwater recharge 56f97577e4b0a6037df06b5a; topographic wetness index 56f97be4e4b0a6037df06b70; STATSGO2 hydrologic soil groups 5728d93be4b0b13d3918a99f; SSURGO soil restrictive layer 572900afe4b0b13d3918aa64; riparian-buffer NLCD 50 m 57855ddee4b0e02680bf37bf and 100 m 64959e63d34ef77fcb01dcb7; percent watershed in waterbodies 57ab4009e4b05e859be1ad26; mean flow-path distance to streams 5d1a1dfbe4b0941bde6025d2
