Reported units: contact time in DAYS; base flow index as PERCENT; water table depth in METRES below land surface; recharge in mm/yr (1951-1980 30-year mean); TWI as ln(a/tan beta); soil groups as percent of catchment per group; restrictive layer as estimated percent presence in the upper 25/35/45/55 cm of agricultural land.
datasets.years: Mostly single-epoch static, but NOT uniformly - the release contains many multi-epoch children (NLCD 2001-2019 across 8 epochs, ClimGRID monthly 1980-2020, housing density 1940-2010, NADP 1985-2014, per-year CDL items). Parent date range 1870-2020.
datasets.access: Unauthenticated HTTPS GET of per-item zipped CSVs (release structure and access VERIFIED; the individual item IDs and units above are UNVERIFIED). Budget for per-item schema discovery - packaging varies, and some items split CAT/ACC/TOT into three separate zips (e.g. BASIN_CHAR_CAT/ACC/TOT at 50-57 MB each) while riparian items are buffer-only.
datasets.license: USGS public-domain data release, free, no authentication. NOT CC0 - no license is stated on the record.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES - full CONUS COMID coverage for all items. Per-item source-layer coverage must be checked individually via the NODATA columns, since the release-wide auditability argument proved vacuous for at least one table.
datasets.whyUseful: This single release covers essentially the entire remaining attribute wishlist - subsurface residence/transit-time proxy (contact time), baseflow index, depth to water table, soil drainage class and hydrologic soil group, riparian buffer fraction, drainage/stream density - all joinable by the same one-hash-lookup COMID path already verified for tile drainage. Availability is fully established.
datasets.howToIncorporate: PRE-REGISTER a set of 3-6 attributes on hydrologic reasoning BEFORE looking at any LOFO score, and evaluate them as a fixed set. Suggested set given the diagnosed deficit: `tot_tiles92` (tile), `tot_contact` (subsurface contact time in days - the transit-time proxy the brief asks for and the one attribute with a genuinely distinct mechanism), `tot_bfi` (base flow index - the groundwater-versus-quickflow partition), and ONE N-input term. Each is created as the TOT_ value at the basin outlet COMID, one hash lookup. Do NOT also add STATSGO2 hydrologic soil groups alongside the tile feature: TOT_HGAD and TOT_HGBD are DEFINED in terms of artificial drainage ('high infiltration rate when artificially drained, very slow infiltration rates when not drained'), making them a tile proxy that is largely redundant with the tile column rather than additive.
datasets.limitations: NO EFFECT SIZE ON NITRATE EXISTS FOR ANY OF THESE ATTRIBUTES anywhere in this corpus, verified or unverified - availability is established, usefulness is entirely untested. The release is a 158-item, thousands-of-columns buffet joinable in one hash lookup, which makes bulk-joining tempting and creates a p >> 19 selection problem where LOFO will select on noise across folds. Structural churn risk: parent provenance records '2026-03-26: The structure of this data release has been updated to support migration to a new USGS data system', which is almost certainly what broke the parquet copies; pin files locally. -9999 has two distinct meanings (100% no coverage in NODATA columns; disconnected from the routing network in ACC_/TOT_ value columns, 9,967 CONUS rows). Individual item IDs and units above are UNVERIFIED.

refuted.originalClaim: AgTile-US's 86.03% CONUS / 91.1% Iowa validation accuracy means an Iowa basin tile fraction carries roughly 9% pixel-level misclassification, and a per-basin aggregate would average much of that out, making basin-level tile fraction a low-noise attribute.
refuted.status: REFUTED - the numbers are verbatim-exact but the inference fails on three independent grounds.
refuted.why: (1) POSITIVES-ONLY VALIDATION. All 16,000 ground-truth points are tile-drained locations; the authors 'limited the tile drainage ground-truth identification mostly to fallow croplands where the tile drainage signature is easily detectable' and list 'uncertainty in croplands without tile drainage' as a primary limitation. There is no confusion matrix, no kappa, no user's accuracy, and 86.03 + 13.97 = 100.00 exactly. These are PRODUCER'S ACCURACY (recall) on a detectability-biased positive subsample, not balanced overall accuracy. The false-positive rate is unreported and unmeasurable from this design - a map that over-painted tile across untiled cropland would score identically. So '~9% pixel-level misclassification' is wrong: it is ~8.9% OMISSION among visually confirmed tiled parcels plus an unknown commission rate. (2) IN-SAMPLE. The same points that report accuracy also set the model's 20% slope threshold ('To validate the AgTile-US AND to set the upper limit of slope in the geospatial model, we have manually identified 16000 ground-truth points'). Separately, the -0.35% agreement with county census totals is circular, since those totals are the calibration target. (3) DECISIVE - WRONG ERROR STRUCTURE. Aggregation averages INDEPENDENT noise. AgTile-US is not an independent per-pixel classifier; it is a deterministic downscaling that allocates county census totals onto pixels via soil drainage class and slope, so errors are spatially correlated at county scale BY CONSTRUCTION, and an Iowa basin spans few counties. The paper's own stated 19.8% average census error propagates to basin aggregates essentially undiluted. Systematic bias does not average out - it becomes a persistent PER-BASIN bias, which is precisely the between-site term the project is trying to improve. WHAT SURVIVES: the dataset recommendation stands on entirely different grounds (free, static, CONUS, pin-computable, the right feature class), but no pixel-level noise figure may be quoted, and basin tile fraction must not be described as low-noise.

refuted.originalClaim: AgTile-US systematically UNDER-predicts tile area by -18.15%, with worst state errors NM -79.06%, WV -42.38%, MS -15.90%, OK -14.06%, TX -11.53% being cropland underestimates; the bias is worst in intermediate soil drainage classes - precisely the discriminating middle needed for site ranking - and larger for multi-state basin tails.
refuted.status: PARTIALLY REFUTED - digits correct, labels inverted, and both stated consequences are null for Iowa.
refuted.why: LABEL ERROR: NM -79.06%, WV -42.38%, MS -15.90%, OK -14.06%, TX -11.53% are AgTile-US TILE-AREA underestimates versus census, NOT cropland underestimates. The paper's NLCD-2016 cropland deficits are CONUS -18.15%, WV -92.00%, NM -27.45%. 'SYSTEMATICALLY UNDER-PREDICTS' OVERSTATES: AgTile-US is area-constrained to county census totals and lands at -0.35% CONUS-wide; underestimation occurs only where the NLCD mask exhausts candidate cells before the county total is met, which is why every affected state is outside the Corn Belt. CONSEQUENCE (i) IS NULL: no Iowa basin drains NM, WV, MS, OK or TX - Iowa's out-of-state tails are MN, IL, MO, NE, SD and WI, none flagged, and the flagged states collectively hold under 0.11 Mha of tile. CONSEQUENCE (ii) IS UNSUPPORTED: 'worst in the discriminating middle' is the claimant's hypothesis, not the paper's - the paper reports only that the 13.97% missed points concentrate in SSURGO categories 3-5 and gives no category-stratified error rate. Iowa tile sits predominantly in the drainage categories AgTile captures best (>98% accuracy in poorly/very poorly drained soils at <=1% slope), so exposure in the study region is small. REPLACEMENT LIMITATION: the real constraint is not low bias but within-county PLACEMENT noise plus the inherited 19.8% census error - heteroscedastic, worse for small single-county basins, partly averaging out for multi-county basins - and a RESOLUTION CEILING, since basin tile fraction is substantially a reallocation of county-level truth.

refuted.originalClaim: AgTile-US is downloadable free with NO authentication including via the Google Earth Engine asset, and its CC-BY 4.0 license makes it shippable in a deployed product with per-pin reduceRegion calls and no local raster storage.
refuted.status: REFUTED FOR THE GEE PATH - valid only for the Figshare path.
refuted.why: The auth-free and commercially-shippable properties are true of the Figshare download (confirmed by anonymous HTTP 206 range download of AgTile-US-TIFF.zip) and INVALID for Earth Engine. EE requires a Google account and an Earth-Engine-registered Google Cloud project (i.e. authentication), and Google's FAQ states Earth Engine 'is free for noncommercial use' while directing commercial or operational applications to paid Cloud pricing - a deployed public-facing product IS an operational application. The CC-BY 4.0 license governs the raster, not the platform serving it. Additional corrections: the GEE asset is an ee.Image, not an ImageCollection, and it is a third-party community mirror maintained by the sat-io project with no persistence guarantee from NCAR or Google. The 'no local raster storage' selling point is also backwards for this deployment target: the CONUS GeoTIFF is 126 MB zipped and trivially vendored, whereas a 30 m reduceRegion over a large multi-state NLDI basin is a seconds-to-minutes call subject to EE timeouts sitting on the critical path of every map-pin request. RECOMMENDED PATH: bulk-download from Figshare once, clip to the Iowa-plus-upstream footprint (uncompressed CONUS is ~14.9 GB, so clip before storing), compute basin tile fraction locally. Reserve GEE for prototyping. Note also that the commonly cited gee-community-catalog.org page does NOT itself contain the Figshare DOI or mention CC0 metadata - it cites only the Sci Data paper DOI - so those specifics must be attributed to the Figshare API and the paper.

refuted.originalClaim: The USGS 'Select Attributes for NHDPlus Version 2.1' release is licensed CC0 1.0 Universal; every one of its 158 attribute tables supplies three spatial aggregations (CAT_/ACC_/TOT_) plus NODATA in a single table; all attributes are static single-epoch snapshots; and the NODATA columns directly fix the project's inner-join undercount by reporting coverage explicitly instead of silently dropping cells.
refuted.status: REFUTED ON FOUR COUNTS - the release is still recommended, but each of these specifics is wrong.
refuted.why: (1) NOT CC0. The ScienceBase `rights` field is null for both parent and tile items and no 'CC0' / 'Creative Commons' / 'public domain' / 'license' string appears in either JSON or the FGDC XML; accconst is 'None' plus a fitness-for-use disclaimer. It is free and unauthenticated and USGS works are public domain by default, but CC0 is an inference the source does not support. (2) THREE AGGREGATIONS IS WRONG - there are FOUR spatial components (reach catchment, riparian buffer zone, network-accumulated catchment, network-accumulated riparian buffer), and 158 counts ITEMS not tables; packaging varies, with some items splitting CAT/ACC/TOT into three separate zips and riparian and ClimGRID items shipping only one aggregation each. (3) NOT ALL STATIC - many children are multi-epoch (NLCD across 8 years, ClimGRID monthly 1980-2020, housing density 1940-2010, NADP 1985-2014, per-year CDL), which is a bonus rather than a defect but makes the blanket statement false. (4) THE NODATA ARGUMENT IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT WAS CLAIMED, AND MUST BE CHECKED PER TABLE. For the Early90s tile table the columns are informative but the VALUE is written 0.0 where NODATA is 100 - so a naive join silently yields zeros, exactly the undercount failure the claim said the dataset fixes; it fixes it only if you explicitly filter on NODATA. For the TILES92 table the NODATA columns are identically 0.0 with no -9999 anywhere, so they carry no coverage diagnostic at all and the auditability argument is vacuous. Also corrected: column names are CAT_TILES92/ACC_TILES92/TOT_TILES92, NOT the CAT_TILES_Early90s naming (which belongs to the other table and to SPARROW), so ingest code written from the original claim would KeyError; file sizes are 11.5 MiB zipped / 133 MiB uncompressed, not 13 MB / 154 MB; the member is a comma-delimited .txt, not a .csv; and the FGDC XML labels the third variable 'ACC_TILES92' twice, so schemas must be parsed from the CSV header.

refuted.originalClaim: AgTile-US authors state the product 'does not represent spatial or temporal changes in drainage installation'.
refuted.status: REFUTED AS A QUOTATION - the meaning is right, the quotation is fabricated.
refuted.why: This sentence is not in the paper. The paper's temporal caveat reads 'The data deliver a static representation of U.S. tile drainage for the year 2017.' The spatial caveat is separate and different: 'each 30-m grid identified as tile drained is entirely tile drained', i.e. presence/absence only, with no sub-pixel drainage density. The operational conclusion - static basin attribute only, no time-varying tile signal, and drained AREA rather than drainage DENSITY - is correct and unaffected. Do not reproduce the quoted sentence.

refuted.originalClaim: AgTile-US is 'not an independent observation of tile drainage', being purely a deterministic function of SSURGO drainage class, slope and cropland - so a basin tile fraction is strongly collinear with those inputs and adds nothing beyond them.
refuted.status: PARTIALLY REFUTED - too absolute in both directions.
refuted.why: The pixel ALLOCATION is pure downscaling, as claimed, and the collinearity warning is operationally sound: do not add AgTile fraction AND SSURGO drainage class AND mean slope as three independent features. But two things are wrong. (a) ONE GENUINELY EXOGENOUS OBSERVATION ENTERS: the USDA county tile acreage is farmer-reported survey data, and the paper states 'thresholds of slope and soil drainage properties were estimated separately for each county'. Two counties with identical soils, slope and cropland but different reported acreage get different thresholds and different tile fractions. So basin tile fraction is f(soils, slope, cropland, COUNTY CENSUS ACREAGE), not a deterministic function of the first three - and that last term is exactly the kind of between-site static information the project lacks. Within a county AgTile variation is fully redundant; BETWEEN counties it carries real information, and Iowa basins span many counties, so the between-county component is where any genuine gain would come from. (b) INDEPENDENT VALIDATION EXISTS and was omitted (16,000 photo-interpreted points, 86.03% CONUS, Iowa 91.1% on 5,253 points) - though per the primary refutation above it is positives-only recall and partly in-sample, so it should be described as point-validated with a county-total mass-balance constraint, not as unvalidated. Minor precision fixes: the soil input is GRIDDED SSURGO (gSSURGO) v2.0 resampled to 30 m, not vector SSURGO, and the D-loop terminates when the county target is exceeded, so D=1 is a search floor rather than a step every county reaches.

refuted.originalClaim: (TIER-3 CLAIM CONTRADICTED BY VERIFIED EVIDENCE) AgTile-US 'underestimates tile drainage by -18.15% CONUS-wide relative to the census totals'.
refuted.status: CONTRADICTED BY TIER-1 - the verified claim wins.
refuted.why: The -18.15% figure is the NLCD-2016 CROPLAND MASK deficit relative to the USDA census, not AgTile-US's tile-area error. AgTile-US's aggregate deviation from the census it was calibrated to is -0.35% CONUS-wide and better than -0.25% across the tile-drained Midwest. Any tier-3 statement describing -18.15% as a tile-area underestimate should be discarded. Similarly, the tier-3 characterization of 86.03% as 'CONUS-scale validation accuracy' must be replaced by the verified reading: producer's recall on a positives-only, detectability-biased sample that also calibrated a model parameter.

refuted.originalClaim: (TIER-3 CLAIM CONTRADICTED BY VERIFIED EVIDENCE) The Nakagaki 2016 CONUS early-1990s tile product and the USGS attribute release are licensed CC0 1.0 Universal.
refuted.status: CONTRADICTED FOR THE PARENT RELEASE; UNRESOLVED FOR NAKAGAKI.
refuted.why: Verification of the parent USGS attribute release found NO license declared anywhere - `rights` is null and no CC0 or Creative Commons string appears in JSON or FGDC XML. Since the Nakagaki tile products are distributed through the same ScienceBase infrastructure, the CC0 attribution circulating for them should be treated as unverified by default. The practical position is unchanged - USGS-authored works are public domain under 17 U.S.C. 105 and access is free and unauthenticated - but the specific string 'CC0 1.0 Universal' should not be cited without checking the individual record.

refuted.originalClaim: (UNRESOLVED SOURCE CONFLICT, NOT A REFUTATION) The Jones et al. (2019) Ambio paper on nine western-Iowa watersheds.
refuted.why: The corpus gives this same paper (same PMC article, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6722160/, same Ambio 48:1143-1153 pagination) under two different DOIs: 10.1007/s13280-018-1137-5 and 10.1007/s13280-019-01150-9. Neither was verified. Resolve the DOI before citing. All substantive claims from this paper are tier-3 unverified regardless.

uncovered: THE ENTIRE EFFECT-SIZE HALF OF THE RESEARCH QUESTION. Every candidate number (David 2010 tile=17%; Jones 2019 manure p<0.01; Schilling & Libra slope 0.11; Pandit 2025 Shapley ranking) is tier-3 unverified. STREAM / DRAINAGE DENSITY as a nitrate control. TOT_STRM_DENS and TOT_STREAM_LENGTH appear in a tier-3 attribute inventory, so the DATA plausibly exists in the USGS release, but no study of any tier relates drainage density to Corn Belt nitrate and no effect size exists.

RIPARIAN BUFFER AND WETLAND FRACTION. The only signal is Pandit et al. (2025) reportedly ranking wetland cover 3rd by Shapley magnitude - tier-3, paywalled, magnitudes explicitly not retrievable. The correct follow-up paper was IDENTIFIED but never retrieved: Schilling & Libra (2003), 'Relation of baseflow to row crop intensity in Iowa', Agriculture Ecosystems & Environment 101(2-3):205-214, DOI 10.1016/j.agee.2003.09.015. No effect size of any kind, in any tier.

SUBSURFACE RESIDENCE / TRANSIT TIME. Dataset reportedly available (contact time in days, ScienceBase item 56f96fc5e4b0a6037df06b12; unsaturated-zone travel time UNSAT_TT; transmissivity TRANSM - all from a tier-3 attribute inventory). ZERO studies relating any of these to stream nitrate were found in either tier. This is arguably the most mechanistically distinct untested attribute and it is entirely unsupported by evidence.

SSURGO SOIL DRAINAGE CLASS AND HYDROLOGIC SOIL GROUP AS DIRECT NITRATE PREDICTORS. Datasets available, but they enter this corpus only as INPUTS to the tile products or as a redundancy warning against them. No source of any tier reports their independent partial effect on cross-site nitrate.

USDA NASS AG CENSUS COUNTY TILE ACREAGE AS A STANDALONE LAYER. The assignment explicitly asked to check this. It appears in the corpus ONLY as a calibration input to AgTile-US and to the Nakagaki products - it was never located, verified, or specified as a directly downloadable county table with a URL, access mechanism and license. Given that this county acreage is the ONLY exogenous observational content in AgTile-US, obtaining it directly (2017 and 2022 Census of Agriculture, county 'land drained by tile' acreage) may be a better-value target than the derived rasters, and is an obvious follow-up.

SUGG (2007), 'Assessing catchment-wide drainage in the United States'. Named explicitly in the assignment. Never retrieved directly. It enters only indirectly, as the reported county-acreage source underlying the Nakagaki 2016 CONUS product. Its own content, method and any effect sizes are unexamined.

TILE-WEIGHTED N SURPLUS (the interaction the assignment asked about). The only relevant signal is David et al. (2010) reportedly finding that runoff x fertilizer-N explained 76% of spatial variation while additive net-N-input was NOT a reliable predictor - tier-3, in-sample, and its runoff term is a DISCHARGE quantity unavailable at an ungauged pin. Pandit et al. (2025) reportedly report a wetness-dependent export fraction (19+/-4% of surplus overall; 42+/-24% in wet years vs 6+/-6% in dry years for Midwestern states) that would mechanistically motivate a surplus x wetness interaction - also tier-3 and paywalled. NOTE THE PROJECT'S OWN NEGATIVE RESULT: antecedent moisture + rain x surplus interactions have ALREADY been tested here and were a wash for REG with only +0.017 PR-AUC for CLF. No verified basis for retrying this exists.

WHETHER A BASIN TILE FRACTION IS CONDITIONALLY INFORMATIVE GIVEN LAT/LON. This is the single most decision-relevant unknown in the angle and NO evidence bears on it either way. Multiple verifiers independently flagged it as the likely reason a tile feature could return null (Iowa tile concentrates in the Des Moines Lobe; lat and lon are already the #2 and #3 permutation-importance features), but nobody has measured the correlation. It is cheap to compute from data already in hand and should be the FIRST step, before any model run.

POST-2017 N-INPUT CONTINUATION. Convergent tier-3 evidence says no product extends past 2017 (Falcone terminates 2017; the 2002-2017 USGS release terminates 2017; gTREND is published as 1930-2017). NONE of this was verified. The proposed workaround - rebuilding a 2022 manure-N layer from USDA NASS QuickStats county livestock inventories times Gronberg & Arnold coefficients times published 2017 weight factors (cattle 1.152, hogs 1.117, sheep 1.078, broilers 1.374, chickens 1.295, turkeys 1.425) - is tier-3 and was never tested, and it carries a documented and growing disclosure-suppression burden concentrated in exactly the high-confinement counties that matter most for Iowa nitrate.

NUMERIC ATTRIBUTIONS FROM THE TWO MOST RELEVANT MODERN PAPERS. Pandit et al. (2025) Shapley magnitudes and non-linear threshold values, and Gorski et al. (2024) per-attribute permutation importances including TILE_DRAIN, are all in paywalled or Cloudflare-blocked figures. Only rank orders and directional statements were extractable, and even those were never verified. Obtaining these two full texts is the highest-value single action for this angle - both are reported to be gold OA or USGS-authored, so an author request or an institutional route should succeed.

SCHILLING & LIBRA (2000) EXPLAINED VARIANCE. The r^2 for the row-crop regressions could not be obtained from any open source (Wiley, USGS pubs page, ProQuest and ResearchGate all HTTP 403). Only p<0.0003 and slope 0.11 are confirmed, and even those are tier-3. How much cross-site variance row-crop percentage actually explains in Iowa therefore remains unknown - which matters, because that attribute is already in the feature set.

ANY SPATIALLY-HELD-OUT NUMBER FOR ANY STATIC-ATTRIBUTE MODEL IN THE CORN BELT. Every candidate effect size in this angle comes from an in-sample cross-sectional regression (David 2010 n=153, Jones 2019 n=9, Schilling & Libra 2000 n=25) or from a within-site temporal holdout (Gorski 2024). The ONE reported spatially-held-out number in the whole corpus is Pandit et al.'s median KGE 0.18 - unverified, paywalled - and it is a discouraging one. No verified spatially-held-out benchmark exists that is comparable to this project's LOFO AUC 0.820.
